title: One-to-one: runtime tactics & pre-brief
content:
Purpose: prep for 1:1 with Eng Lead (Leah) — align on short list of runtime tactics we can ship in the next 6 weeks that materially improve tail latency and reduce unit cost for bursty workloads. Keep it tactical: feature gating, quick experiments, clear owners.

Meeting length: 30 min (10m sync, 15m decisions, 5m actions).

Topline context (two-sentence recap to open the call):
- Traffic has 2x weekday midday bursts from PLG onboarding flows; observed 99.9p latency spikes on hosted API and Dedicated during those windows.  
- PM ask: prioritize mitigations that recover p99 to below 350ms for short prompts while keeping cost impact <5% on steady-state.

Agenda (my preferred order):
1) Quick metric check (2–3m) — confirm Leah sees same signals.
2) Tactics triage (12m) — decide which tactics to push to fast-experiment vs. runway.
3) Canary plan for rollout (8m) — who owns, instrumentation, rollback criteria.
4) Open blockers & decisions (5m) — infra/infra-cost approvals, privacy gating for Private installs.

Notes + prep points (what I want to surface):
- Metric snapshot to have on call: 7d rolling p50/p95/p99, error rate, estimate steady vs burst token throughput. (I have a quick spreadsheet link in linked_artifacts).
- Current SLOs: 200ms p50, 250ms p95, 350ms p99 for hosted-api baseline (reminder). Dedicated customers have relaxed p99 to 450ms but expect predictability.
- Cost sensitivity: product wants <5% incremental ops spend. Ops is ok with short-term burst overprovisioning limited to 12% if it is transient.
- Safety: Private customers require we preserve KMS boundary; any cache-sharing proposal must be per-tenant and KMS-agnostic.

Tactics candidate list (quick notes, pros/cons, rough effort):
A) Adaptive tiny-batches for short requests (fast-experiment)
   - What: reduce default batch size for requests under 256 tokens, but dynamically expand when idle capacity.
   - Why: reduces head-of-line blocking for short prompts during bursts.
   - Risk: more kernel launches -> CPU/GPU overhead; need metric on per-token cost.
   - Effort: small (2w eng + 1w validation).

B) Prefix KV caching (fast-experiment on hosted only)
   - What: opportunistic in-memory cache of the most common prompt prefixes across customers on hosted API; per-tenant safe mode for Private/Dedicated.
   - Why: large wins for PLG onboarding flows that repeat system prompts.
   - Risk: privacy/regulatory for Private; collisions/thrashing cost.
   - Effort: medium (3w + infra changes).

C) Lightweight quantized-path for short sequences (runway)
   - What: route short sequences to a quantized kernel variant optimized for 8-bit inference reducing GPU memory pressure.
   - Why: cost reduction on steady state, reduces queuing under constrained capacity.
   - Risk: potential quality regression; requires evals.
   - Effort: medium-high (4–6w + eval pipeline).

D) Stealth canary: region-level weight-based fallbacks (fast-experiment)
   - What: when a region exceeds capacity, automatically spill to compatible lower-cost model variant in same region for a % of requests.
   - Why: avoids global capacity spikes and cross-region latency.
   - Risk: model behavior divergence; must have quality hooks and per-route policies.
   - Effort: small (2w config + observability).

E) Routing priority tokens for interactive flows (runway)
   - What: allow a short-lived token that marks requests as "interactive" to get higher scheduling priority for N seconds.
   - Why: improves p99 for UX-sensitive paths.
   - Risk: abuse vector; needs rate limiting and quota accounting.
   - Effort: small (2–3w + quota plumbing).

My prioritized shortlist (what I want to propose in the meeting):
- Fast experiments: A (adaptive tiny-batches), D (stealth canary), E (routing priority tokens). Goal: ship at least one to production in 4 weeks.
- Runway items: B (prefix KV cache) gating on privacy model; C (quantized path) for Q2.

Decision points for Leah during call:
- Which tactic to greenlight for immediate fast-experiment? (I prefer A + D together because they target different bottlenecks).
- Approve metric/alerting set for canary (p50/p95/p99, tail error rate, delta-cost-per-1M-tokens).
- Confirm privacy constraint: prefix caching only for hosted unless customer explicitly opts-in.

Canary & rollback plan (draft):
- Canary window: 48h with a 10% traffic split to start, monitor p99, error delta and cost.
- Rollback triggers: p99 > baseline + 30% sustained for 10m OR error rate > baseline + 0.5% OR quality regression flagged in evaluation harness.
- Owner: eng lead (Leah) owns rollout orchestration; PM (Kiran) owns customer comms and gating.
- Observability: new dashboard tile + automated Slack alerts to #prod-incidents + email to SRE leads.

Open blockers to resolve before next week:
- Infra budget approval for short-term burst buffer (Ops needs estimate; action: Diego to produce cost delta by EOD Friday).
- Privacy review for prefix cache (Security review required for hosted->private divergence).
- Small infra patch necessary for priority token plumbing (estimate 2d infra lead time).

Post-meeting action slate (what I'll capture live and follow up):
- [ ] Decision: tagged tactics (who, what, when) — capture in Jira (owner: Kiran) — due: 2026-03-16.
- [ ] Diego: cost delta spreadsheet for burst buffer and tiny-batch overhead — due: 2026-03-13.
- [ ] Leah: greenlight one fast-experiment and assign eng owner + PR number — due: 2026-03-12 (ideally during or immediately after call).
- [ ] Security: quick privacy guidance on prefix cache for Private customers (contact: Maya in security) — due: 2026-03-15.
- [ ] Observability: add canary dashboard tile and the two synthetic checks (p99 and model-quality hook) — owner: SRE — due: 2026-03-18.

Personal notes to self (non-actionable reminders):
- Keep language precise when talking to sales/CS: emphasize predictable p99 wins, not absolute elimination of spikes. Customers care about consistency and clear rollback.
- If Leah asks about model regression risk, have the small eval plan ready (10 prompts representative + automated diff).
- Avoid promising cross-region spillovers for Dedicated without explicit capacity ordering.

Scratch space (quick raw ideas — dump here during call):
- Could we test a tiny-batch config that biases microbatching across origins? (ie per-customer microbatch repeater) — hazard: fairness.
- Idea: temporary per-route soft-quotas to smooth bursts originating from single-token fanout.
- Would prefer to prototype A in dev cluster with synthetic burst generator to validate cost delta.

End of doc — will convert to meeting notes and populate Jira tasks after call.
